findings.evidence: RPC is single-shot request/response, never retried at the wire layer: ClientConnectionRpc.call returns RpcResult<unknown> with caller-supplied signal only (packages/client/connection/src/rpc.ts:71-76). The only retry machinery is provider-owned for LLM generation and is confined to transient codes (packages/llm/llm/src/retry-policy.ts:25-34 DEFAULT_RETRYABLE_CODES, 79-110 resolveRetryPolicy; packages/llm/llm-retry/src/index.ts:177-208 fail-code gate). No Idempotency-Key header or dedup table exists in the gateway (packages/api/gateway/src/index.ts:107-226) or the SSE/WS carrier (packages/client/connection/src/websocket-downlink.ts:1-152). The only `idempoten` occurrences in src are Cordis-disposer and replay semantics, not request dedup.
findings.next_step: Acceptable while the /api surface is request/response with no wire-level retry. If the carrier (websocket-downlink.ts) or the python JSON-RPC runtime is ever extended to auto-retry lost client calls, append an `Idempotency-Key` to ClientRequest and store accepted rpcIds in a short TTL set (server rejects duplicates with `already-accepted`).

findings.evidence: The browser-trust fence on /api is explicitly NOT an auth layer: `Network reachability and authentication stay out of scope ... this fence is not an auth layer.` (packages/client/connection/src/api-request-trust.ts:12-13, repeated :94-108). WebServer bind host is a closed union including `0.0.0.0` (packages/host/webserver/src/index.ts:47 `host: '127.0.0.1' | '0.0.0.0'`, :60-63 Schemastery schema). No bearer/api-token exists in the HTTP carrier (packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts:2114 declares `Host visibility is the authorization boundary` — capability by session-id, not API authentication). The RpcErrorCode map (packages/host/apiproxy/src/api/rpc.ts:31-101) has no `unauthorized`/`forbidden`/auth code. Passing the fence requires Host in loopback union trustedHosts (api-request-trust.ts:96-122): a native LAN attacker controlling a `0.0.0.0`-bound instance can set Host to any configured trustedHosts entry and reach model+fs+subprocess execution with no token, since browsers cannot set Host but curl/scripts can. Cross-site/Origin fences (api-request-trust.ts:108-122) mitigate browser CSRF only. STRIDE Spoofing+EoP materializes only when a non-loopback bind is chosen; the default loopback mitigates this to single-user local access.
findings.next_step: Keep loopback the default (already so) and audibly refuse `host=0.0.0.0` unless `trustedHosts` is an explicit non-empty set; on any non-loopback bind mint a startup secret token written to owner-only `$DSH_HOME/.api-token` and require an `Authorization: Bearer` header on /api (adding `unauthorized` to RpcErrorCode).
